title: Connect an LLM provider with an API key
prompt:
# Story: Connect an LLM provider with an API key

- **Story**: XXX-llm-provider
- **Created**: 2026-11-03
- **Status**: Draft

## Story

As a team member, I want to choose where the AI comes from (Claude on Amazon Bedrock, Claude on the Anthropic API, or Azure OpenAI) and
connect it with an API key, so that the project can use the AI service that my team already pays for.

## Acceptance tests

Choosing a provider

- [ ] **Given** Integrations in a project with no connection, **Then** the card "LLM provider" says "Not connected".
- [ ] **Given** the card is opened, **Then** three options show: "Claude on Amazon Bedrock", "Claude on the Anthropic API" and
  "Azure OpenAI". None is selected, no field shows, and Connect is disabled.
- [ ] **Given** the user chooses "Claude on Amazon Bedrock", **Then** the fields are "Amazon Bedrock API key" (placeholder
  "bedrock-api-key-..."), Region ("us-east-1"), Model id ("us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"), Prompt cache lifetime ("5 minutes")
  and Longest answer (4096 tokens).
- [ ] **Given** the user chooses "Claude on the Anthropic API", **Then** the fields are "Anthropic API key" (placeholder "sk-ant-..."),
  Model id ("claude-sonnet-4-6"), Prompt cache lifetime ("5 minutes") and Longest answer (4096 tokens). There is no Region.
- [ ] **Given** the user chooses "Azure OpenAI", **Then** the fields are "Azure OpenAI API key" (placeholder "Key 1 or Key 2 of the
  resource"), Endpoint (placeholder "https://your-resource.openai.azure.com"), Deployment name (placeholder "the name you gave the
  model in Azure") and Longest answer (4096 tokens). There is no Region, no Model id and no Prompt cache lifetime.
- [ ] **Given** a key was typed, **When** the user chooses another option, **Then** the key field is empty, so that a key is never
  sent to a provider it does not belong to.

Connecting

- [ ] **Given** a provider and a valid key, **When** the user presses Connect, **Then** the button reads "Connecting...", and when the
  provider has answered, the card shows the chip "Connected", the provider and the model (for Azure OpenAI, the deployment) and, for
  Bedrock, the Region or, for Azure OpenAI, the endpoint, for example "Claude on the Anthropic API · claude-sonnet-4-6" or
  "Azure OpenAI · my-gpt · your-resource.openai.azure.com". The key field is gone.
- [ ] **Given** an empty key (or only spaces), **When** the user presses Connect, **Then** "Paste the Azure OpenAI API key." (with the
  name of the chosen provider's key) shows and nothing is sent.
- [ ] **Given** Azure OpenAI with an empty endpoint or deployment name, **Then** "Enter the endpoint of the Azure resource." or "Enter
  the deployment name." shows and nothing is sent.
- [ ] **Given** an endpoint that does not start with "https://" or is not a valid address, **Then** "The endpoint looks wrong, for
  example https://your-resource.openai.azure.com." shows and nothing is sent.
- [ ] **Given** a key with spaces inside, **Then** "Paste the key without spaces." shows and nothing is sent.
- [ ] **Given** Longest answer is 100 or 70000, **Then** "Maximum tokens must be a whole number between 256 and 64000." shows and
  nothing is sent.
- [ ] **Given** the provider refuses the key, **Then** the card stays "Not connected", nothing is kept, and the message names the
  provider and says the key was refused, for example "Anthropic refused the key. Check that it is valid and active."
- [ ] **Given** the model id does not exist for the provider (for Azure OpenAI, the deployment does not exist on that endpoint),
  **Then** the card stays "Not connected", nothing is kept, and the message says to check the model id (or the deployment name and
  the endpoint).
- [ ] **Given** the provider cannot be reached, **Then** the card stays "Not connected" and the message says the provider could not be
  reached, with a Connect button that tries again.
- [ ] **Given** a successful Connect, **Then** the short test request is counted in the usage of the project (Costs).

Using the connection

- [ ] **Given** a project connected to Amazon Bedrock, to the Anthropic API or to Azure OpenAI, **When** the user sends a prompt in the
  builder, **Then** the story streams in the same way for all three, and the line with the tokens shows input, output, cache read
  and cache write.
- [ ] **Given** a project connected to Azure OpenAI, **Then** the cache write is 0 and the cache read is what Azure OpenAI reports as
  cached.
- [ ] **Given** a project connected to a provider, **When** the user uses "Improve with AI", the driver assistant or a diagram, **Then**
  the same provider answers.
- [ ] **Given** project A connected to Amazon Bedrock and project B to Azure OpenAI, **Then** each project's requests go to its own
  provider with its own key.
- [ ] **Given** no provider is connected, **When** the user sends a prompt, **Then** the message says "No model is connected for this
  project. Connect one in Integrations."

Changing, switching and removing

- [ ] **Given** a connection, **Then** the card shows the provider, the model and the settings of that provider, and "Key: entered
  here, kept by the backend". No part of the key is shown.
- [ ] **Given** a connection, **When** the user presses "Change settings", **Then** the form of the same provider shows with the
  current values and the key field empty ("Leave empty to keep the current key"). **When** Save with an empty key, **Then** the
  settings are checked with the key that is kept.
- [ ] **Given** a connection, **When** the user presses "Change provider", **Then** the three options show with the note "Connecting
  replaces the current connection (Claude on Amazon Bedrock)." and a Cancel that keeps everything as it was.
- [ ] **Given** the user connects another provider with a valid key, **Then** the card shows the new provider and the key and settings of
  the old one are deleted.
- [ ] **Given** the user connects another provider and the check fails, **Then** the old connection keeps working and nothing of the
  new attempt is kept.
- [ ] **Given** a connection, **When** the user presses "Remove the key", **Then** the card says "Not connected" and the key and settings
  are deleted.

The key stays on the backend

- [ ] **Given** any provider, **Then** the browser sends the key once, to the BWYN backend over its REST API. It never calls a provider,
  and the key is not in the bundle, in the browser storage or in any response to the browser.
- [ ] **Given** the status of a connection is asked for, **Then** the answer has the provider, the model, the settings and whether it is
  connected, and never the key.
- [ ] **Given** the key is refused or the request fails, **Then** the key is not in the error message nor in the logs.
- [ ] **Given** the backend, **Then** these calls (the providers and their settings, connect, status and remove) are in its OpenAPI
  document.

## Business rules and constraints

- There are three providers: Claude on Amazon Bedrock, Claude on the Anthropic API, and Azure OpenAI (the OpenAI models that run in
  the team's own Azure resource). Signing in with an account is not used.
- An API key is the only credential, for all three. Azure OpenAI also needs to know where the resource is (the endpoint) and which
  deployment to call: in Azure the model is reached through a deployment name that the team chose, not through a model id.
- A project has one connection at a time. Every project has its own, with its own key.
- The settings that exist depend on the provider: Region only for Bedrock, the endpoint and the deployment name only for Azure OpenAI,
  and the prompt cache lifetime only for the two Claude providers. Azure OpenAI caches by itself, so there is nothing to choose.
- Bedrock and the Anthropic API start with a default model that the user can change. Azure OpenAI has none, because the deployment
  name is the team's own.
- The endpoint must be an https address. The backend calls only the endpoint that the user entered for that project.
- "Connected" means that the provider answered a short test request (a few tokens) with the key and the settings. Nothing is kept
  otherwise, and a failed attempt never removes a working connection.
- The keys stay on the backend. The rest of BWYN (the prompt, the assistants, the diagrams) does not know which provider is used: it
  asks for a reply and gets the same stream of text, usage and end whichever provider answers.
- Usage is counted as input, output, cache read and cache write for all providers, so that Costs does not change.

## Out of scope

- More than one provider connected to a project at once, a fallback between them, and choosing a provider per feature.
- Other providers (OpenAI directly, ChatGPT, Gemini, local models) and signing in with an account instead of a key.
- A list of the models or deployments of a provider (the user types the model id or the deployment name), and the price in money (Costs counts tokens only).
- How the keys are encrypted at rest on the backend (a decision for an ADR).

## Tasks

- [ ] Define in the backend one way to check a connection and to stream a reply, with the provider, model and settings of a project, and
  keep one connection per project.
- [ ] Move the connect, status and remove of Amazon Bedrock behind it, as REST calls described in the OpenAPI document, without the key
  in any answer.
- [ ] Add the Anthropic API provider: check, streaming, prompt cache lifetime and usage.
- [ ] Add the Azure OpenAI provider: check against the endpoint and deployment, streaming and usage, with the cached tokens as cache read.
- [ ] Check the endpoint (https, valid address) and give clear errors per provider for a refused key, an unknown model or deployment and an unreachable provider, without the key in them or in the logs.
- [ ] Make the builder, the assistants and the diagrams use the connected provider of the project, with the message for a project with none.
- [ ] Replace the Bedrock card with the "LLM provider" card: the three options, the fields of each, the checks of the fields, and the
  connected view.
- [ ] Add "Change settings", "Change provider" (the old connection stays until the new one works) and "Remove the key".
- [ ] Test each provider against a fake provider server, so that no real key is needed.

---

# Reference

Spike: `bwyn-frontend/spikes/home-page/LlmIntegrationCard.tsx` (today's card, Amazon Bedrock only), `builder/bedrockClient.ts` (status,
connect, disconnect, usage and the stream), `server/bedrock.js` (the dev server that checks and keeps the key per project, and streams)
and `Settings.tsx` (Costs, which reads the usage and the status). This story builds on `story-improve-with-ai.md`, which moves the
call to the model to the Spring Boot backend (ADR 0004, documented with OpenAPI, ADR 0010).
